newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rises despite blue chip stagnation.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rises despite blue chip stagnation.

text.p: The Czech PX50 closed 0.24 percent higher on Tuesday but the major issue dominated RPIX stagnated on 1,018.5 suggesting that most of the upward pressure on the broader index was brought by smaller issues.
After solid gains on Monday, in the immediate aftermath of a strong showing in the first round of senate elections by the right, blue chips had mixed fortunes.
Power utility CEZ lost five crowns to 946 and Komercni Banka fell 22 crowns to 2,029. SPT Telecom rose one crown to 2,870 and Ceska Sporitelna gained nine crowns to 313.

Analysts said that the initial euphoria after the election results at the weekend would inevitably subside and that the familar problem of inadequate regulation on the equities market would reassert itself as the main issue concerning investors.

"It is quite likely that many investors had timed their investments to (coincide with) these days. Everyone expected these results but this does not affect the fundamental problem of transparency," said Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka.
In the first round of Senate elections at the weekend, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's right wing Civic Democratic Party (ODS) virtually swept the board.
However, final round run-offs in all but four of the 81 constituencies will take place this coming weekend and the Senate's powers will be broadly limited to those of amendment and delay.

Investors say the Senate itself can have little effect on the underlying problems of inadequate protection for minority shareholders and the lack of transparency in Czech equities trading, which must be addressed by the government.
The Finance Ministry has mooted the idea of setting up a U.S. style Securities and Exchange Commission sometime next year but no concrete plans have yet been laid.
Most trading in Czech equities is conducted on the over-the-counter (OTC) market.
